tier_reason: Upgraded from C: the independent ilgrad/string-index-benchmarks harness pins this repo at commit 92c1b86 (the only commit here), builds it with its own CMake Release flags (-O3 -march=native per CMakeLists.txt; harness/build.sh) and publishes per-cell results in results/frontier-1m-2026-09-26-arz-be75a38.json naming GCC 16.2.1 and an AMD Ryzen 7 5800HS; there C2-FST and C2-MARISA beat the FST and MARISA baselines on most corpora. The repo's own README headline (up to 1.92x / 1.51x) is first-party and its CPU model is not stated.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Authors' README (arXiv 2606.16104): C2-FST up to 1.92x faster and up to 41% smaller; C2-CoCo up to 1.22x faster and up to 46% smaller (against CoCo'); C2-MARISA up to 1.51x faster and up to 46% smaller. Independent rerun at 1M keys on 12 corpora (string-index-benchmarks artifact, derived from page data, rho=0 vs rho=0 lookup latency): C2-MARISA 1.21x to 1.48x faster than MARISA on all 12; C2-FST 1.05x to 1.82x faster than FST on 11 and 0.87x (slower) on opaque; C2-CoCo against the original CoCo-trie is slower on 7 of 8 corpora where both ran (0.78x to 0.92x) and faster only on urls (1.49x). Size: C2-MARISA up to 43% smaller than MARISA (dna) but 13% larger on words; C2-FST up to 36% smaller than FST, 2.5% larger on domains.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: C++20, CMake Release: -O3 -march=native -Wall -pedantic (CMakeLists.txt); independent rerun with GCC 16.2.1
corrections.hardware: Authors: single Intel Xeon Gold core with 25 MB LLC (exact model not stated). Independent rerun: AMD Ryzen 7 5800HS (8 cores / 16 threads, 16 MiB L3), Fedora 44, 2026-09-26
corrections.caveats: Authors' numbers come from the arXiv preprint 2606.16104 (blocked here) and README; they are 'up to' maxima and the CoCo comparison is against CoCo' (a C2-CoCo build with the original CoCo bitvector), not the upstream CoCo-trie. In the independent rerun C2-CoCo is slower than upstream CoCo-trie on most corpora and larger on dna (10.25 vs 6.14 B/key); C2 variants produced no result on the numeric corpus. The independent harness is written by the author of lexindex (a competing dictionary), uses C2's own benchmark.cpp driver for the C2 and FST/CoCo/MARISA baseline rows, and lists C2-CoCo rho=1 as the smallest structure on dna at 10M keys. The listed repo is a one-commit public release copy forked from HardyZ1906/C2; alexztc/C2 redirects here. Vendored baselines keep their upstream licenses.

notes: Repo page confirms MIT, 0 stars, forked from HardyZ1906/C2, single commit 92c1b86 on 2026-06-20 (matches the harness pin). Tier raised to A on the independent string-index-benchmarks artifact; the C2-CoCo speed claim does not hold against upstream CoCo-trie there.

tier_reason: First-party README benchmarks with public code (Cydhra/vers_benchmarks), CPU (Ryzen 9 7950X) and flag (target-cpu=native) stated, but no rustc version and results only as SVG plots without numeric values; comparisons are only against other Rust crates (succinct rank9, rsdict, sucds, bio, fid, indexed_bitvec; RMQ crates), not the C++ SDSL/sux incumbents.

corrections.baseline: Rust crates succinct (rank9), rsdict, bio, fid, indexed_bitvec, sucds (rank9, darray); range_minimum_query and librualg for RMQ; bitm and qwt mentioned but not plotted as winners
corrections.caveats: Compares only against other Rust crates, not SDSL or sux, so it does not beat the named baselines of this category. README states the succinct crate's rank9 substantially outperforms Vers on rank, and qwt is substantially faster for wavelet-matrix style queries. Benchmark repo (Cydhra/vers_benchmarks, 2 stars) has no README and its results are plots, so no numbers were verified; rustc version not stated. The 2 to 3x figure is BMI2/popcnt intrinsics versus Vers without them, not versus a competitor. The simd feature needs AVX-512. Included as shootout context for Rust succinct libraries.

notes: README and repo page match the record (Apache-2.0 OR MIT, 134 stars, last commit 2026-08-10). Tier C stands; claim is qualitative and not against C++ incumbents.
